refuted.title: Ground not known: a main house on higher ground with an ATTACHED lower garage is still 'raised' and drops out of the at-grade cut and the yards' walls reading
refuted.detail: The round-8 fix reads 'raised' from the connected group. That covers a detached shed (its own group) but not the common sloped-site case of a garage attached to the house and stepping down. If any solid touching the house has a lower bottom and nothing sits under the house's footprint, the house counts as a balcony. Probe with no spot grades and the ground unknown or sloped: house box(10,25,35,65,3,33) + attached garage box(35,30,47,50,0,10), main_building=house. Result: building_area readings [covered from above 1240, at the main grade level 240] plus the overhang question, and the front yard loses 'to its walls at ground level' (readings are only 'seen from above' and 'any solid'). 86a3a16 gives the same 1240/240, so this is not a regression. It is the prior finding's pattern ('a solid above the lowest one is raised: the main house on higher ground drops out') still present, now limited to touching solids. The _at_ground docstring says 'a solid above the lowest one is not raised for that alone', and for an attached lower solid it still is. The result is needs review (no false pass), but the question asked is the wrong one: an overhang question about a house that has no overhang.

refuted.prior_ref: With no spot grades and an unknown or sloped ground, any solid above the lowest one is 'raised'
skeptics:
I could not refute this finding. I read packages/model_measurement/model_measurement/measure.py lines 185-216 (_at_ground and _raised_by_shape) and lines 1041-1051 (_connected). When there are no spot grades and grade_known is False, _at_ground (line 201-202) decides whether the solid rests on the ground from `not _raised_by_shape(...)`.

In _raised_by_shape, `under` only counts other solids whose plan overlaps this one by more than TOL in area (line 211). An attached garage that only shares an edge with the house overlaps it by zero area, so `under` is empty. _connected, however, groups solids by plan distance <= TOL (line 1048), so the garage is in the house's group. That makes `lower` True at line 215, and line 216 returns True, so the house counts as raised.

I ran this with the repo venv, using box(10,25,35,65,3,33) for the house and box(35,30,47,50,0,10) for the garage:
- `_raised_by_shape(house, [house, garage])` returned True.
- `_at_ground(house, [house, garage], 0.0, None, False)` returned POLYGON EMPTY, so the house drops out of the at-grade cut.

This contradicts the _at_ground docstring, which says a solid above the lowest one is not raised for that alone. The result is still 'needs review' rather than a false pass, so P2 fits. The reviewer says this pattern was already present at 86a3a16, i.e. pre-existing rather than a regression. I did not re-check that myself. Either way, the code on this branch shows the behavior.

I ran the probe in /home/user/wt/review_pr15: house box(10,25,35,65,3,33) plus attached garage box(35,30,47,50,0,10), main_building=house, with ground_is_flat and grade_elevation removed and no spot grades. It does give building_area readings of 1240 "covered from above" and 240 "at the main grade level" with value=None (needs review). front_yard = 25.0, with only the "seen from above" and "any solid" readings. So the numbers are reproducible. What I don't accept is the claim that this is a defect that contradicts the documented design.

1) measure.py:206-216 `_raised_by_shape` does exactly what its docstring says. With the ground not known, a solid is "raised" if it "overhangs (nothing under its footprint while a solid it touches rests lower: a balcony)". The house touches a lower solid (the garage at x=35, distance 0, so _connected at measure.py:1041-1051 groups them) and nothing is under its footprint. That is the documented balcony rule, applied on purpose.

2) The finding says this goes against the _at_ground docstring at measure.py:185-191 ("a solid above the lowest one is not raised for that alone"). It doesn't. The house is not called raised just for sitting higher. It is called raised for the extra documented reason that it touches a lower solid and has nothing under it. "For that alone" is kept.

3) With no ground data, the drawing alone cannot tell a house on a 3 ft step-up next to a lower garage from a 25x40 part cantilevered past a ground-level solid on a flat site. The geometry is the same. Without ground information, deciding either way is a guess. The code instead gives needs review with both readings (1240 vs 240) and the overhang question. That follows principle 4 (never a false pass), and the finding admits no false pass happens. front_yard still returns 25 ft from the above-view readings, and the reading that is left out is consistent with the solid being treated as possibly raised.

4) The finding also says 86a3a16 gives the same result, so this is not a regression from the branch's change.

At most this is a wording or UX nit: the question shown is an overhang question when the real doubt is whether the house sits on the ground. It is not a correctness bug in the changed code, and the behavior is deliberate and documented.
